summary: Madhusudan Kaul Shastri was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Director (attested 1918–1934) and Superintendent (attested 1943–1945) at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir.
Madhusudan Singh Vats (1896–1972) worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He succeeded Rakhal Das Banerji (Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay).

Sinologist and art historian Maggie Bickford studied at Bennington College (c. 1961–1965), Yale University (c. 1974–1977), and Princeton University (c. 1981–1987). She was Professor of East Asian Studies at Brown University (1993) and a Member at the Institute for Advanced Study (c. 1999–2000).

Active in Indology, history, and archaeology, Maha Chakri Sirindhorn studied at Chitralada School, Chulalongkorn, Srinakharinwirot, Peking University, AIT, and Silpakorn University (M.A. in Oriental Epigraphy, 1977–1979) under Satyavrat Shastri.

Mahadev Govind Ranade (1842–1901) was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Elphinstone College, the University of Mumbai, and Government Law College, Mumbai. In 1885, he founded the Maharashtra Girls Education Society.

Mahasi Sayadaw (1904–1982) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. Trained by Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw U Narada, Aletawya Sayadaw, and Thelon Sayadaw, he served as Abbot at Mawlamyine Monastery (1941) and resident teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha (1947, 1949).

Mahesh A. Deokar is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. At Savitribai Phule Pune University, he has served as Professor (attested 2011) and Head of department (attested 2020–2021).

Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya (1836–1906) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1882, 1894, and 1914).

Mahinda Deegalle is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned degrees from Peradeniya, Harvard, and Chicago, studying under Diana L. Eck, Wendy Doniger, and Frank E. Reynolds. He held posts at Bath Spa, Harvard, McGill, and Colgate.
Mahiro Ito (born 1967) is a Buddhist studies scholar who succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021 and serves as a professor at Bukkyo University.
Maho Iuchi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Otani University by 2008 and was a visiting researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies in 2010.
Mai Mishiro is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She was affiliated with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011) and Waseda University (attested 2016).

Makio Takemura (born 1948) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ryomin Akizuki. He served at Mie University, the University of Tsukuba, and as president of Toyo University (2009–2020).
Makio Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Otani University by 2009. He served there as an assistant professor (attested 2010–2012) and remained affiliated in 2022.

Makoto Funaoka (born 1946) is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and history. Educated at Meiji University, he lectured at the Open University of Japan and Komazawa University, and became professor emeritus at Hokkai-Gakuen University (1993–2017).

Makoto Kitada is an Indology and linguistics scholar. Kitada completed doctoral studies at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and held an attested post at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute from 2008 to 2010.

Makoto Nagai (1881–1970) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology with a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo, Toyo, Nihon, and Kamakura Women's University, and president of Chuo Shoka Junior College.

Makoto Yoshimura (born 1969) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University (c. 1994–2000) and served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University (c. 2003).
Malati J. Shendge (born 1934) is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale, R. D. Vadekar, and Akira Hirakawa.

Malcolm David Eckel (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. Educated at Oxford and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, he held posts at Harvard, Middlebury, and Boston University (1990–2024), alongside visiting roles at Michigan and Sydney.
